sections.heading: A — Driving definitions
sections.markdown:
## A — Driving definitions
The cover identifies this Wyoming driver manual as the 2021 edition [A01].
The Wyoming Department of Transportation Driver Services Program issues the state's driver licenses [A02].
This dossier covers driving definitions for the noncommercial passenger-car applicant path.
The handbook says its written test draws on the manual and covers sign recognition, signals, markings, driving laws, safety, crash prevention and vehicle equipment [A03].
No unambiguous written-test question count, passing threshold, bank size or time limit has been verified; these official exam fields remain unknown (verify WY-SEC15-EXAM, WY-SEC15-PASS).
The current issuer page links this edition but warns that print-date information may be outdated; effective date and present applicability need confirmation (verify WY-SEC15-FRESH).
Practice mastery is product policy from the pinned learning loop; it does not establish an official test threshold.

sections.heading: B — Driving definitions
sections.markdown:
## B — Driving definitions
Audience: first-time applicants preparing for a Wyoming noncommercial passenger-car written knowledge test, with driving definitions as this section's subject.
Learning level: beginner. The source scope is the mapped physical pages; explanations use original wording and retain every actor and exception.
Passenger-car applicants distinguish the handbook's road, vehicle, licensing and safety terms. Motorcycle and off-road operating instructions remain outside this regular passenger-car scope.
This dossier teaches the handbook source; it does not confer a license, replace required exams or establish current eligibility independently.

## C — Driving definitions
FACT_ID: sec15-F01 | anchor: A01
Authorized emergency vehicles include fire, police and ambulance vehicles and others authorized by statute. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0091]

FACT_ID: sec15-F02 | anchor: A01
The glossary defines a bicycle as a human-powered vehicle with two tandem wheels, excluding scooters and similar devices. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0091]

FACT_ID: sec15-F03 | anchor: A01
The handbook classifies bicycles as vehicles that may use Wyoming public roads. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0091]

FACT_ID: sec15-F04 | anchor: A01
The handbook recommends a correctly fitted, Consumer Product Safety Certified bicycle helmet even though it says a helmet is not legally required. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0091]

FACT_ID: sec15-F05 | anchor: A01
The glossary's blind spots lie near the rear corners on both sides and are not visible in rearview mirrors. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0091]

FACT_ID: sec15-F06 | anchor: A01
Turn the head to view the glossary's blind-spot areas. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0091]

FACT_ID: sec15-F07 | anchor: A01
BAC stands for Blood Alcohol Concentration and refers to alcohol in the bloodstream. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0091]

FACT_ID: sec15-F08 | anchor: A01
Brakes are the devices used to stop a vehicle. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0091]

FACT_ID: sec15-F09 | anchor: A01
A critical object is anything that could require slowing, accelerating or turning, including a person, vehicle or animal. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0091]

FACT_ID: sec15-F10 | anchor: A01
A crosswalk is a place where people may legally cross a street or highway. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0091]

FACT_ID: sec15-F11 | anchor: A01
A crosswalk may be marked or unmarked. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0091]

FACT_ID: sec15-F12 | anchor: A01
For an unmarked crosswalk, the glossary uses imaginary lines connecting sidewalks across the roadway. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0091]

FACT_ID: sec15-F13 | anchor: A01
DWUI means operating a vehicle while under the influence of alcohol or a controlled substance. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0091]

FACT_ID: sec15-F14 | anchor: A01
The glossary's emancipated minor is at least 17 and is or was married, serves in the United States military, or has district-court emancipation. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0091]

FACT_ID: sec15-F15 | anchor: A01
An emancipated minor may request that status on a Wyoming license by applying to the department and paying the required fee. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0091]

FACT_ID: sec15-F16 | anchor: A01
A traffic gap is enough open space between vehicles for another vehicle to enter safely. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0091]

FACT_ID: sec15-F17 | anchor: A01
A helmet is protective headgear. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0091]

FACT_ID: sec15-F18 | anchor: A02

Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0092]

FACT_ID: sec15-F19 | anchor: A02
An intersection is the area where streets or highways meet or cross. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0092]

FACT_ID: sec15-F20 | anchor: A02
A lane is a roadway section for one line of vehicles. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0092]

FACT_ID: sec15-F21 | anchor: A02
A median separates roadways and may consist of grass, concrete or other material. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0092]

FACT_ID: sec15-F22 | anchor: A02
Riding on, over or across a median is unlawful under the glossary's rule. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0092]

FACT_ID: sec15-F23 | anchor: A02

FACT_ID: sec15-F24 | anchor: A02

FACT_ID: sec15-F25 | anchor: A02

Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0092]

FACT_ID: sec15-F26 | anchor: A02
A moving violation involves control or lack of control while a motor vehicle is moving and results in a conviction. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0092]

FACT_ID: sec15-F27 | anchor: A02
A moving-violation conviction can include driving contrary to a corrective-lens or outside-mirror restriction. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0092]

sections.heading: C2 — Driving definitions
sections.markdown:
## C2 — Driving definitions
FACT_ID: sec15-R01 | anchor: A01
The multipurpose-vehicle definition requires an identifying number, at least four wheels, weight from 300 to 3,000 pounds and a permanent upright seat at least 24 inches above ground. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0093]

FACT_ID: sec15-R02 | anchor: A01
A multipurpose vehicle must be registered and plated for street or highway operation. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0093]

FACT_ID: sec15-R03 | anchor: A01
A multipurpose vehicle may not operate on interstate highways and is subject to slow-moving-vehicle requirements. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0093]

FACT_ID: sec15-R04 | anchor: A01
The handbook permits a multipurpose vehicle to be driven under any driver-license class. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0093]

FACT_ID: sec15-R05 | anchor: A01
A No-Zone is a heavy vehicle's side or directly rearward area where another vehicle is invisible to its driver. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0093]

FACT_ID: sec15-R06 | anchor: A02
A pedestrian vehicle is self-propelled equipment designed exclusively for people with a physical disability. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0094]

FACT_ID: sec15-R07 | anchor: A02
The glossary limits pedestrian-vehicle width to 48 inches. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0094]

FACT_ID: sec15-R08 | anchor: A02
A reinstatement fee is required before a suspension or revocation can be lifted and the driving privilege restored. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0094]

FACT_ID: sec15-R09 | anchor: A02
The residency definition's presence clause specifies 120 days or more in the jurisdiction. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0094]

FACT_ID: sec15-R10 | anchor: A02
Being registered to vote in Wyoming is an alternative included in the handbook's resident definition. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0094]

FACT_ID: sec15-R11 | anchor: A02
Applying for public assistance from Wyoming is an alternative included in the resident definition. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0094]

FACT_ID: sec15-R12 | anchor: A02
Holding a valid Wyoming resident hunting or fishing license is another stated resident-definition alternative. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0094]

FACT_ID: sec15-R13 | anchor: A02
Revocation terminates the privilege to drive. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0094]

FACT_ID: sec15-R14 | anchor: A02
A roadway is the street or highway portion ordinarily used for driving. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0094]

FACT_ID: sec15-R15 | anchor: A02
The shoulder lies beside the traveled highway and can be paved or gravel. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0094]

FACT_ID: sec15-R16 | anchor: A02
A shoulder accommodates stopped vehicles and helps highway drainage. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0094]

FACT_ID: sec15-R17 | anchor: A02
A space cushion separates the vehicle from others ahead, behind and beside it. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0094]

FACT_ID: sec15-R18 | anchor: A02
Suspension temporarily removes driving privileges, with return possible after time, specified requirements or both. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0094]

FACT_ID: sec15-R19 | anchor: A02
Total stopping distance includes travel while deciding to stop, reacting and braking until the vehicle fully stops. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0094]

FACT_ID: sec15-R20 | anchor: A02
WYDOT is the state agency responsible for Wyoming driver licensing. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0094]
